title: Make it virtual
description:
`makeNoise` takes any `Animal` by reference and asks it to speak. Pass it a `Dog` and it still says `"..."`: the call is decided at compile time from the type of the reference, which is `Animal`.

Make `speak` **virtual** in the base class, and mark the two derived versions `override`. Then the call is decided at run time from what the object really is.
hints: Add `virtual` in front of `speak` in `Animal`, and write `override` after the parameter list in `Dog` and `Cat`. The compiler then checks that they really override something.
unitTests:
TEST("each animal speaks for itself through a base reference") { CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Dog{}), "Woof"); CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Cat{}), "Meow"); CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Animal{}), "..."); }
TEST("and through a base pointer") { const Dog d{}; const Animal* p{ &d }; CHECK_EQ(p->speak(), "Woof"); }

grading.unitTests:
TEST("each animal speaks for itself through a base reference") { CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Dog{}), "Woof"); CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Cat{}), "Meow"); CHECK_EQ(makeNoise(Animal{}), "..."); }
TEST("and through a base pointer") { const Dog d{}; const Animal* p{ &d }; CHECK_EQ(p->speak(), "Woof"); }
